binders: An arbitrary type E equipped with an additive commutative group structure and a real-module structure.
An E-valued sequence of cell averages U : Nat → E.
An E-valued sequence physicalEdgeFlux : Nat → E.
A numerical-flux operator numericalFluxFromCellAverages which, given an entire Nat-indexed cell-average sequence, returns an E-valued flux at every natural-numbered edge.
hypotheses: The flux scale is strictly positive: 0 < fluxScale.
For the fixed cell-average sequence U, the numerical flux agrees with the supplied physical edge flux at every edge: numericalFluxFromCellAverages(U,edge) = physicalEdgeFlux(edge).
conclusions: The proposition repeats the assumed positivity 0 < fluxScale.
There exists an updated E-valued cell-average sequence U′ : Nat → E.
The proposition repeats, for every edge, the assumed equality between the numerical flux evaluated on U and physicalEdgeFlux.
For every cell i, U′ᵢ = Uᵢ − fluxScale · (Fᵢ₊₁ − Fᵢ), where Fₑ = numericalFluxFromCellAverages(U,e).
For every natural number N, the sum over the first N updated cells satisfies Σ_{i=0}^{N−1} U′ᵢ = Σ_{i=0}^{N−1} Uᵢ − fluxScale · (F_N − F_0).
Using the numerical/physical flux equality, the same prefix balance can be rewritten with boundary term physicalEdgeFlux(N) − physicalEdgeFlux(0).
mathematical_definitions: Edge i is the left edge of cell i and edge i+1 is its right edge according to the update's indexing convention.
The local update is U′ᵢ = Uᵢ − λ(Fᵢ₊₁ − Fᵢ), with λ = fluxScale.
Finset.range N is the set of cells {0,1,…,N−1}.
The finite-prefix balance follows by telescoping: summing Fᵢ₊₁ − Fᵢ from i = 0 through N−1 leaves only F_N − F_0.
All sums, differences, and scalar products are taken in the real module E, so the statement covers scalar, vector, or other real-module-valued conserved quantities.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Let E be any real module with additive inverses, let U₀,U₁,… be cell averages, and let a numerical-flux operator assign an E-valued flux Fₑ to every edge from the entire cell-average sequence. Assume a positive real flux scale and assume that, for this fixed sequence, every numerical edge flux equals a supplied physical edge flux. Then one can define updated cell averages by the conservative flux-difference rule U′ᵢ = Uᵢ − fluxScale(Fᵢ₊₁ − Fᵢ). The numerical/physical flux equality is retained, and for every finite prefix of N cells the internal fluxes cancel, giving Σ_{i=0}^{N−1} U′ᵢ = Σ_{i=0}^{N−1} Uᵢ − fluxScale(F_N − F_0). Thus the change in a finite prefix is exactly the scaled difference between its right and left boundary fluxes.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition genuinely proves the algebraic finite-prefix telescoping balance for every cellCount, including cellCount = 0.
It does not derive numerical/physical flux agreement. That equality is assumed for every edge and merely repeated in the conclusion.
The physicalEdgeFlux sequence is arbitrary and is not required to arise from a physical conservation-law flux, interface states, geometry, or a Riemann solver.

The numerical-flux operator may depend nonlocally on the entire cell-average sequence. No two-cell locality, consistency, symmetry, continuity, conservation-law interpretation, or computability condition is imposed.
The agreement hypothesis applies only to the single fixed sequence cellAverages, not uniformly to every possible input sequence.
The updated sequence is obtained directly from a pointwise formula. Its existential construction does not establish analytical solvability, stability, convergence, accuracy, or regularity.
Although uniqueness is not stated, the pointwise equality determines updatedCellAverages uniquely by function extensionality.
The index set is the half-infinite natural-number lattice. The theorem gives balances only for finite prefixes beginning at cell 0, not for arbitrary intervals or for an infinite total sum.
No boundary condition is imposed at edge 0, and F_0 remains as an explicit left-boundary contribution.
The finite-prefix identity is a local algebraic conservation statement, not a claim that the prefix sum is invariant. It is invariant only when its two boundary fluxes agree.
fluxScale is only required to be positive. No upper bound, CFL condition, or interpretation as time step divided by cell width is formalized.
Positivity of fluxScale is not needed for the algebraic telescoping identity itself; it is an extra premise repeated unchanged in the conclusion.
There is no time index or iteration. The proposition describes one explicit update only.
No cell geometry, cell volume, edge orientation, mesh spacing, or dimensional units are represented.
E may be the trivial real module, in which case all flux and conservation equalities are automatic.
Because physicalEdgeFlux can always be chosen to equal the numerical flux for the fixed input sequence, the agreement premise alone imposes little mathematical restriction.
ambiguities: The adjective physical in physicalEdgeFlux has no formal physical content beyond the assumed equality with the numerical flux.
fluxScale may be intended to represent a time-step-to-cell-width ratio, but formally it is only a positive real scalar.
The edge convention is inferred from the formula: edge i is the left boundary and edge i+1 the right boundary of cell i.
The proposition does not specify whether E represents a scalar conserved quantity, a finite vector of conserved variables, or another real-module-valued state.
No semantics are given for how numericalFluxFromCellAverages computes an edge flux from the global state.
